review_evidence: Reviewed all 33 primary Lean files; the repository contains three competing formalizations of Smullyan knights-and-knaves puzzles with extensive custom set/propositional theorem libraries and solved puzzle statements.
The root and Build modules are import/navigation surfaces and are retained; no lossless noise subtree was established.
summary: Reviewed Raymond Smullyan KnightsAndKnaves and retained the complete formal puzzle/theorem corpus.

review_evidence: File contains 3 example theorems with hypotheses modeling knight/knave statements as propositional equivalences
First example (lines 16-69) has a complete proof of (Alice ∧ ¬Ted) using case analysis on excluded middle
Second example (lines 88-115) has a complete proof of ¬A ∧ B ∧ C for a 3-person puzzle
Third example (lines 117-140) is a partial proof with sorry for a variant with 4 propositions
File imports SmullyanKnightsAndKnaves.logic but is not a pure import aggregator — it declares and proves its own theorems
summary: Inspected the single Lean file containing formalizations of Raymond Smullyan's Knights and Knaves logic puzzles. The file includes a complete formalization of puzzle #201 with 6 inhabitants and a full proof, plus two additional puzzle formalizations (one complete, one partial with sorry). All content consists of formal mathematical statements and proofs in Lean.
